title: "Climate GSK studies data"
author: "Laura Andrea Barrero Guevara"
date: '2022-08-31'
---

####################################################################################################
Purpose: This script processes spatial data from various GSK studies to extract Köppen-Geiger Climate 
(KGC) classifications and latitude-based classifications for each location. It then aggregates this 
data to assign a dominant (unique) classification to each country in each study.
Classifications considered: 
- kgc_1: Climate, Köppen classification, 1st level with 5 main groups (A-tropical, B-dry, 
  C-temperate, D-continental, E-polar)
- kgc_2: Climate, Köppen classification, 2nd level with 14 combinations with the main groups (
  Af-rainforest, Am-monsoon, Aw-savanna-dry winter, As-savanna-dry summer, BW-arid-desert, 
  BS-semi-arid steppe, Cw-dry-winter, Cf-no-dry-season, Cs-dry-summer, Dw-dry-winter, 
  Df-no-dry-season, Ds-no-dry-summer, ET-tundra, EF-ice-cap)
- kgc_3: Climate, Köppen classification, 3rd level for main groups B, C and D (BWh-hot, BWk-cold,
  BSh-hot, BSk-cold, Csa-hot-summer, Csb-warm-summer, Csc-cold-summer, Cwa-hot-summer, 
  Cwb-warm-summer, Cwc-cold-summer, Cfa-hot-summer, Cfb-warm-summer, Cfc-cold-summer, Dsa-hot-summer, 
  Dsb-warm-summer, Dsc-cold-summer, Dsd-very-cold-summer, Dwa-hot-summer, Dwb-warm-summer, 
  Dwc-cold-summer, Dwd-very-cold-summer, Dfa-hot-summer, Dfb-warm-summer, Dfc-cold-summer,
  Dfd-very-cold-summer)
- reg_2: Latitude, north and south-hemisphere
- reg_3: Latitude, temperate north, tropics, and temperate south
- reg_4: Latitude, temperate north, tropics north, tropics south, and temperate south 
- reg_6: Latitude, temperate north, subtropical north, tropics north, tropics south, subtropical 
  south, and temperate south

Functions Used: 
- `fun_data_kgc.R`: Retrieves the KGC classification for a location based on its coordinates.

Output (for each study): 
- `stu_kgc_{stu_id}.rds`: Processed KGC classification data frame for the study.
- `stu_clusters_{stu_id}.rds`: Processed data frame containing classifications based on KGC and 
  latitude for all locations in the study and the selected classification for each country in the 
  study. 
- `stu_clusters.rds`: Final aggregated data frame containing classification information for all 
  studies and countries. 
####################################################################################################

# Load packages, themes, directories, and functions
```{r}
rm(list = ls())
source("00_pck.R")
source("fun_data/fun_data_kgc.R")
library(nasapower)
library(tidygeocoder)
dirs$processed_clim <- glue("{dirs$processed}/03_stu_climate")
```

# Load the spatial data for included studies
```{r}
stu_included <- readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_included.rds")) %>%
  filter(included == TRUE)

stu_spatial <- sapply(stu_included$study, function(x) {
  readRDS(glue("{dirs$processed}/02_stu_spatial/stu_spat_{x}.rds"))}, simplify = F)
```

# Extract KGC classification for each location in each study =======================================
```{r}
stu_kgc <- sapply(stu_included$study, function(x) {
  pomp::bake(file = glue("{dirs$processed_clim}/stu_kgc_{x}.rds"), 
             dir = getOption("pomp_archive_dir", dirs$pomp), {
    fun_data_kgc(dat = stu_spatial[[x]])
  })}, simplify = F)
# Please note that using the kgc package creates conflicts with tidyverse, best to restart session.

bind_rows(stu_kgc)
```

# Assign clusters ==================================================================================
First assign clusters for each location (kgc and latitude) and then select dominant (unique) 
classification for each country

```{r}
stu_clusters <- sapply(stu_included$study, function(x) {
  pomp::bake(file = glue("{dirs$processed_clim}/stu_clusters_{x}.rds"), 
             dir = getOption("pomp_archive_dir", dirs$pomp), {
    
    # Assign clusters based on KGC classification --------------------------------------------------
    stu_kgc[[x]] %>%
      mutate(
        # Extract first character for a broad classification
        kgc_1 = str_sub(ClimateZ, 1,1),
        # Extract first two characters for a finer classification
        kgc_2 = str_sub(ClimateZ, 1,2),
        # Use full ClimateZ for the most detailed classification
        kgc_3 = ClimateZ) %>%
      
    # Assign clusters based on latitude data -------------------------------------------------------
      # Define 6 latitude-based groups (merging Arctic and temperate zones into a single 
      # temperate group)
      mutate(reg_6 = case_when(
        lat > 35 ~ "1_Temperate",
        lat <= 35 & lat > 23.5 ~ "2_Subtropical",
        lat <= 23.5 & lat > 0 ~ "3_Tropical",
        lat <= 0 & lat > -23.5 ~ "4_Tropical south",
        lat <= -23.5 & lat > -35 ~ "5_Subtropical south",
        lat <= -35 ~ "6_Temperate south")) %>%
      # Define 4 latitude-based groups (merging Arctic, temperate, and subtropical into a single 
      # temperate group)
      mutate(reg_4 = case_when(
        lat > 23.5 ~ "1_Temperate",
        lat <= 23.5 & lat > 0 ~ "2_Tropical",
        lat <= 0 & lat > -23.5 ~ "3_Tropical south",
        lat <= -23.5 ~ "4_Temperate south")) %>%
      # Define 3 latitude-based groups (distinguishing temperate from tropical regions)
      mutate(reg_3 = case_when(
        lat > 23.5 ~ "1_Temperate",
        lat <= 23.5 & lat > -23.5 ~ "2_Tropical",
        lat <= -23.5 ~ "3_Temperate south")) %>%
      # Define 2 latitude-based groups (north and south)
      mutate(reg_2 = case_when(
        lat > 0 ~ "1_North",
        lat <= 0 ~ "2_South")) %>%
      
    # Aggregate classification data at the country level -------------------------------------------
      select(study, country, llid, starts_with("kgc"), starts_with("reg")) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = c(starts_with("kgc"), starts_with("reg")), 
                   names_to = "cluvar", values_to = "cluvar_name_i") %>%
      arrange(study, country, cluvar, cluvar_name_i) %>%
      # Calculate the total number of centers per country and classification variable
      group_by(study, country, cluvar) %>%
      mutate(country_tot = n()) %>%
      # Calculate the number and proportion of centers per classification within a country
      group_by(study, country, cluvar, cluvar_name_i) %>%
      mutate(cluvar_tot_i = n(),
             cluvarp_i = cluvar_tot_i/country_tot) %>%
      # Identify the classification with the highest proportion within each country
      group_by(study, country, cluvar) %>%
      mutate(cluvarp = max(cluvarp_i),
             cluvar_name = cluvar_name_i[which.max(cluvarp_i)]) %>%
      ungroup()
  })}, simplify = F)
```

# Combine cluster for all studies and countries into a single data frame and save as RDS
```{r}
stu_clusters <- bind_rows(stu_clusters) %>%
  distinct(study, country, cluvar, cluvar_name, cluvarp) %>%
  # Add median longitude and latitude for each country
  left_join(group_by(bind_rows(stu_spatial), study, country) %>%
              summarise(lon_med = median(lon), lat_med = median(lat), .groups = "drop"),
            by = join_by(study, country)) %>%
  rename(c = cluvar_name, p = cluvarp) %>%
  # Reshape data to have separate columns for each classification variable and proportion
  pivot_wider(names_from = cluvar, values_from = c(c, p), 
              names_glue = "{cluvar}_{.value}", names_vary = "slowest") %>%
  rename_all(~str_remove_all(., "_c"))

# Save the clusters data as RDS 
saveRDS(stu_clusters, glue("{dirs$processed_clim}/stu_clusters.rds"))
```

# Extract time series of climate with NASA Power ===================================================

# Extract raw data 
```{r}
library(nasapower)
library(tidygeocoder)
library(ratelimitr)

# List of locations 
llid_df <- bind_rows(stu_spatial) %>%
  distinct(llid, study, country, lon, lat) 

# Function to extract data 
fun_nasapower <- function(llid_name = "112157_Poland_ll001", lon = 18.0126907, lat = 53.133902) {
  nasapower::get_power(
    community = "ag",
    lonlat = c(lon, lat),
    pars = c("RH2M","T2M","T2MDEW","PS","CLOUD_AMT"),
    dates = c("1998-01-01", "2018-12-31"),
    temporal_api = "daily") %>%
    # To dataframe
    as.data.frame() %>% 
    # Tidynames and variables
    rename_with(~tolower(paste0("clim_",.x))) %>%
    mutate(llid = llid_name,
           lon = lon, 
           lat = lat) %>%
    select(-c(clim_lon, clim_lat))
}

# Extract raw data from list of locations (2630)
try_np = FALSE
if(try_np) {
  for (i in 1:1000) {
    try(
      walk(llid_df$llid, limit_rate(function(x) {
        pomp::bake(file = glue("{dirs$raw}/nasapower/nasapower_{x}.rds"), dir = "",{
          fun_nasapower(llid_name = x, 
                        lon = llid_df[llid_df$llid == x,"lon"][[1]],
                        lat = llid_df[llid_df$llid == x,"lat"][[1]])
        })
      }, rate(n = 40, period = 60)))
    ) 
  }
}

llid_df
```

# Summarise data per week and save it 
```{r}
stu_nasapower <- pomp::bake(file = glue("{dirs$processed_clim}/stu_nasapower.rds"), dir = "",{
  lapply(llid_df$llid, function(x) {
    readRDS(glue("{dirs$raw}/nasapower/nasapower_{x}.rds")) %>%
      # Obtain week
      mutate(week = week(clim_yyyymmdd)) %>%
      select(-c(clim_year, clim_mm, clim_dd, clim_doy, clim_yyyymmdd)) %>%
      # Obtain mean per week
      group_by(llid, lon, lat, week) %>%
      summarise(across(starts_with("clim_"), mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pivot_longer(starts_with("clim_"), names_to = "clim") %>%
      # Normalized mean per week
      group_by(llid, lon, lat, clim) %>%
      mutate(value_norm = value - mean(value)) %>%
      ungroup()
  }) %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    left_join(llid_df, by = join_by(llid, lon, lat)) %>%
    select(study, country, llid, lon, lat, week, clim, value, value_norm)
})
```

# Summarise data per week  
```{r}
stu_nasapower <- pomp::bake(
    file = glue("{dirs$processed}/stu_nasapower.rds"), dir = "", { 
        bind_rows(stu_nasapower_l) %>%
        # Obtain week
        mutate(week = week(clim_yyyymmdd)) %>%
        select(-c(clim_year, clim_mm, clim_dd, clim_doy, clim_yyyymmdd)) %>%
        # Obtain mean per week
        group_by(study, country, lon, lat, week) %>%
        summarise(across(starts_with("clim_"), mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
        pivot_longer(starts_with("clim_"), names_to = "clim") %>%
        # Normalized mean per week
        group_by(study, country, lon, lat, clim) %>%
        mutate(value_norm = value - mean(value)) %>%
        ungroup()
})
```
